title: WHAT IF YOU COULD SWITCH OFF SLEEP?

segments.line: Mo can't figure out how you're always this awake.
He's on his third energy drink.
Teachers start calling on you just to watch you get it right.
Day three. You still don't feel tired.
You write the answer on the board. The right answer…
Then, on the stairs, the world blinks.
Mo catches you. He says you were asleep. Standing up.
You don't remember any of it.
It has a name: a microsleep.
Your brain grabs a few seconds of sleep, and it doesn't ask first. That's real.

shots.note: the class at dusk: the board full of formulas, every one solved; you at your desk, hand already up, sure
quiz papers slap down one after another, each stamped A+

shots.line: Mo can't figure out how you're always this awake.
shots.note: Mo slumped on the desk next to you, eyes half shut; you upright, wide awake, eyes glowing

shots.line: He's on his third energy drink.
shots.note: three energy-drink cans on Mo's desk; his hand drags the third one in; gulp
you, nothing on your desk, a cool little shrug; a tag: 0

shots.line: Teachers start calling on you just to watch you get it right.
shots.note: the teacher at the board points at you; a kid turns to look; you answer, smug

shots.line: Day three. You still don't feel tired.
shots.note: the wall calendar: day 3 gets its red cross; DAY 3
you, still glowing, one slow heavy blink; the glow flickers; a flicker of worry

shots.line: You write the answer on the board. The right answer…
shots.note: you at the board writing the answer in chalk, confident
the board: the answer is to YESTERDAY's question, a big red X; kids laugh; you, oops

shots.line: Then, on the stairs, the world blinks.
shots.note: you walk down the stairs (walkPhase), mid-step: the screen cuts to black for 12 frames, silence
you pitch forward off the step, arms flailing

shots.line: Mo catches you. He says you were asleep. Standing up.
shots.note: Mo grabs you under the arms; you hang there dizzy, stars circling

shots.line: You don't remember any of it.
shots.note: you, still held up by Mo, dazed: you don't remember any of it; the stars fade

shots.line: It has a name: a microsleep.
Your brain grabs a few seconds of sleep, and it doesn't ask first. That's real.
shots.note: a day as a bar: AWAKE runs, a few seconds of SLEEP cut in without asking; REAL
